items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: Monty came in that same night and played with us.

ctx.x: No. Not with Sarah. With Al Hibbler. But right after Sarah, right after I left Sarah, and that was not a very good way to leave anybody— Sarah had a husband at that time, his name was C.B. Atkins. And he left us stranded. Didn’t pay us the last week in the hotel in Las Vegas, and didn’t get an airplane ticket for us to get out of there. So they just left. Well of course we stayed and we called the union back in New York and Hy Jaffe was the treasurer at that time. And he called Sarah’s house and he told C.B. if…

good experience. But then when that ran dry I went to work with Al Hibbler. And Al Hibbler and I were in Miami, Florida, playing in a hotel/bar type place that had a restaurant. This was in 1965. And as a matter of fact this was the same year I met Monty Alexander. Monty came in that same night and played with us. I told him I said, “Look, this is my number, you come up to New York I’ll get you some work. You play too good to be down here, man, come up to New York.” He was 18 years old I think and he came up.…
Well those were active days too, in civil rights.
